steps.tx: **Malignant spinal cord compression** presents with back pain and leg weakness rapidly. **Steroids** must be started immediately before imaging confirms the diagnosis in these patients. **MRI** of the whole spine is the urgent investigation of choice for this emergency. **Radiotherapy** decompresses the cord when surgery is not feasible or not advisable.

steps.tx: **Superior vena cava obstruction** causes facial swelling with distended neck veins. **Stenting** is the fastest relief when symptoms threaten airway or brain function. **SVC stenting** is the definitive relief for malignant obstruction in many cases. **Salbutamol** has no role here despite its inclusion in some listing errors confusion.
steps.say: Superior vena cava obstruction causes facial swelling with distended neck veins. Stenting is the fastest relief when symptoms threaten airway or brain function. Anticoagulation alone does not relieve obstruction without stenting in many cases. Supportive care is required until definitive therapy is available in every patient.

steps.tx: **Hypercalcaemia of malignancy** presents with polyuria, constipation and confusion in many cases. **Saline hydration** is first line therapy for moderate hypercalcaemia in most patients. **Furosemide** has no routine role unless fluid overloaded in these sick patients. **Calcium gluconate** reverses membrane effects during severe symptomatic hypercalcaemia in cardiac patients.

Furosemide has no routine role unless fluid overloaded in these sick patients. Calcium stabilisation is required for membrane effects during severe symptomatic hypercalcaemia in cardiac patients.

steps.tx: **Tumour lysis syndrome** follows chemotherapy in bulky highly proliferative tumours. **Potassium** rise with hypocalcaemia is the classic biochemical pair in this syndrome. **Rasburicase** clears uric acid rapidly in high risk tumour lysis cases. **Allopurinol** or **febuxostat** prevents uric acid rise in moderate risk disease in many protocols.

Rasburicase is the treatment for high risk tumour lysis cases rapidly. Allopurinol or febuxostat prevents uric acid rise in moderate risk disease in many protocols.

steps.tx: **Leukostasis** causes dyspnoea and neurologic symptoms with very high white counts. **Sodium bicarbonate** alkalinises urine during tumour lysis management in selected cases. **Sodium chloride** hydration is the mainstay of lysis prevention in many protocols globally. **Insulin** with glucose shifts potassium intracellularly during lysis hyperkalaemia management in these patients.

steps.tx: **Neutropenic sepsis** is fever with very low neutrophil counts during chemotherapy. **Azathioprine** and **mercaptopurine** cause myelosuppression when overdosed in many patients. **Venetoclax** neutropenia needs growth factor or dose delay in many protocols. **Dexamethasone** is not antimicrobial therapy despite its common use in many regimens.
steps.say: Neutropenic sepsis is fever with very low neutrophil counts during chemotherapy. Azathioprine and mercaptopurine cause myelosuppression when overdosed in many patients. Venetoclax neutropenia needs growth factor or dose delay in many protocols. Empiric antibiotics are required immediately for every neutropenic fever case.

steps.tx: **Pericardial tamponade** from malignancy causes hypotension with muffled heart sounds. **Pericardiocentesis** is therapeutic and diagnostic in malignant tamponade cases. **Pleural effusion** with dyspnoea responds to drainage and pleurodesis in many cases. **Ascites** control combines sodium restriction with diuretic therapy in these patients.

Pleural effusion with dyspnoea is treated by drainage and pleurodesis in many cases. Ascites control combines sodium restriction with diuretic therapy in these patients.

steps.tx: **Tumour lysis** needs electrolyte monitoring every 6 hours in high risk cases. **Sodium chloride** saline diuresis is preferred over loop diuretics in many lysis protocols. **Electrolytes** panels track potassium, phosphate and calcium trajectory serially in these patients. **Calcium gluconate** is given only for symptomatic hypocalcaemia in lysis management practice.

Electrolyte panels track potassium, phosphate and calcium trajectory serially in these patients. Calcium stabilisation is required only for symptomatic hypocalcaemia in lysis management practice.

steps.tx: **Hyperleukocytosis** with counts above 100 × 10³ needs leukapheresis in symptomatic cases. **Cytoreduction** with supportive measures is a bridge when leukapheresis is unavailable in many settings. **Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)** complicates promyelocytic leukaemia emergency in these patients. Blood product support precedes chemotherapy in coagulopathy cases in many protocols.

steps.tx: **SVC stenting** relieves symptoms within hours in most malignant obstruction cases. **Radiotherapy** addresses tumour mass when stenting is not feasible in these patients. **Anticoagulation** failure is common without stenting in malignant SVC obstruction cases. **Dexamethasone** reduces oedema during radiotherapy for cord compression in many protocols.

steps.tx: **High-yield for the exam** ends the emergency summary clearly. Remember steroids before MRI for cord compression, stenting for SVC obstruction relief and rasburicase for high risk tumour lysis. Saline hydration is first line for hypercalcaemia while insulin glucose shifts potassium inward. Neutropenic sepsis needs immediate empiric antibiotics in every case.
steps.say: High-yield facts are the points the examination asks most often in these presentations. Steroids before MRI are required for cord compression management. Stenting is the fastest relief for SVC obstruction cases. Rasburicase is the treatment for high risk tumour lysis. Saline hydration is first line for hypercalcaemia cases.
